title: Extra heads follow the designated head
statement: Let $P$ be a finite Turing machine over an alphabet $A$ with $k$ work tapes, let $l$ be a natural number, choose a designated work-tape index $h<k$, a finite data-state set $D$ with initial state $d_0$, and any visit function of the specified type. For every input word $x$, time $t\in\mathbb N$, and extra-tape index $i<l$, the head position of extra tape $i$ in the decorated machine after $t$ steps from its initial configuration equals the position of head $h$ at that time.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ is finite and has decidable equality
$P$ is a finite Turing machine over $A$
The visit function has the stated type
$i$ is an extra-tape index less than $l$
replaced:
Let a machine $P$ over an alphabet $A$ be decorated by any data transducer with $l$
extra tapes and designated head $h$. For every input word $x$, every time
$t \in \mathbb{N}$, and every extra-tape index $i < l$, the head position of the
$i$-th data tape of the decorated machine after $t$ steps equals the head position of
the designated schedule head $h$ at the same time — including at all times after
halting. Consequently no data-selected write can alter a head trajectory.
